statement: Zoe sells lemonade. If she charges $p$ dollars per cup, she sells $100 - 20p$ cups in a day, for any price $p$ from $\$1$ to $\$5$. Each cup costs her $\$1$ to make, and she makes only the cups she sells. What is the greatest daily profit she can make, in dollars?

choices.misconception: I assumed she always makes $100$ cups, so I subtracted $\$100$ from her largest possible sales, $\$125$, and got $25$.
I first found the price that brings in the most money, $\$2.50$, and then worked out the profit at that price: $50 \times 1.50 = 75$.
I found the best price, $\$3$, but forgot to subtract the cost of the cups, so I gave her sales of $40 \times 3 = 120$.
I found the most money she can take in, $50 \times 2.50 = 125$, and forgot about the cost of making the cups.

hints: Her profit on each cup is the price minus $\$1$.
Profit $= (p - 1)(100 - 20p) = 20(p - 1)(5 - p)$. The two factors $p - 1$ and $5 - p$ always add up to $4$.
Two numbers with a fixed sum have the largest product when they are equal, so take $p - 1 = 5 - p = 2$.

solutions.reliable: Profit is the number of cups times the profit per cup: $(100 - 20p)(p - 1) = 20(5 - p)(p - 1)$. The factors $5 - p$ and $p - 1$ add up to $4$, and two numbers with a fixed sum have the largest product when they are equal, so the best choice is $5 - p = p - 1 = 2$, which is $p = 3$. She sells $40$ cups at a profit of $\$2$ each, for $\$80$. Nearby prices do worse: at $p = 2.5$ the profit is $50 \times 1.5 = 75$, and at $p = 3.5$ it is $30 \times 2.5 = 75$.
